paper.title_en: Eliminating Incompatibility in Quantum Multiparameter Estimation with Antiparallel Probes
paper.abstract_en: The simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters is fundamentally constrained by complementarity and measurement incompatibility, which limits the sensitivity of quantum measurement devices by preventing the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) from being saturated. We show that antiparallel probe configurations can overcome this limitation when the dynamics of the parameter encoding preserve the said configurations. We characterise the quantum channels that satisfy this requirement and establish conditions under which such configurations exist and can saturate the SLD-CRB without compromising the quantum Fisher information, leading to a metrological advantage. For qubit probes, we prove that this advantage is present if and only if the encoding channel is unital. We extend this analysis to the two probe, finite dimensional qudit case by considering derivative reversal and transpose map based probe states, as well as more general multiprobe configurations. For each of these cases, we identify conditions under which an advantage exists. Our results establish connections between channel symmetries, probe configurations and the attainability of multiparameter precision limits.
